title: News consumers are wary of most AI use in local news, a Chicago-based report finds
tldr: A Medill survey finds audiences distrust AI in news-gathering, signaling that transparency and human authorship still matter to readers. Concrete data on how people react to AI in journalism.
why_fresh: new survey data on AI trust
angle: Why 'human-made' is becoming a trust signal in content, and how brands can label AI use honestly.

title: Human-centered content gets a boost from connectioneering
tldr: Adobe argues for engineering human connection into content workflows rather than optimizing purely for scale. Directly aligned with people-over-polish content thinking.
angle: How to design 'connection' into content ops without losing the human texture that makes it resonate.

title: 2026 employee advocacy stats to secure C-level buy-in
tldr: Sprout compiles fresh data to help communicators sell employee advocacy programs to executives with proof rather than passion. Strong ammo for EGC advocates.
angle: Building the business case for employee-generated content: the metrics that actually move the C-suite.

title: It's about social media discoverability, not followers
tldr: Sprout argues the follower-count era is over; discoverability via search and recommendation now drives reach. A meaningful shift in how audiences find content.
angle: Why chasing followers is dead and how discoverability rewrites social content strategy.

title: How women athletes are betting on the creator playbook
tldr: Women athletes are using content creation to build personal brands, grow fandom and close salary gaps. A rich real-world case of human-centered creator strategy.
angle: How under-resourced talent turns personal content into leverage — lessons for any brand's people-first strategy.

title: AI is eating website traffic, websites are blocking AI – and reliable information is getting harder to find
tldr: The web's link-based social contract is collapsing as AI crawlers take content without referring traffic, and sites retaliate by blocking. Existential for content publishers.
angle: What content strategists should do when AI breaks the traffic-for-content bargain.

title: What Domino's campus strategy reveals about influencing communities
tldr: Domino's local, personal campus activation shows how Gen Z influence is becoming hyper-local rather than mass-scale. A concrete campaign breakdown.
angle: The shift from mass reach to local trust: what campus marketing teaches about community-led content.

title: New York Times training editor: Take these four steps before you roll out new things
tldr: An NYT deputy editor on why saying 'no to new' and disciplined rollout beats constant novelty. Useful change-management thinking for content teams.
angle: Why restraint beats novelty in editorial ops — a framework for rolling out content changes people adopt.

title: Is There Life After Substack?
tldr: Puck examines whether newsletter writers can build sustainable businesses beyond Substack's platform lock-in. Key reading on newsletter and creator business models.
angle: Owning your audience: the risks of building a content business on someone else's platform.

title: Reach Cuts 220 Jobs as Google Traffic Falls, Shifts to Subscriptions
tldr: UK publisher Reach lays off 220 as search traffic dries up and pivots to direct subscriber relationships. A stark case study in the post-search content business model.
why_fresh: live restructuring driven by search decline
angle: When Google traffic vanishes: what publisher layoffs signal for owned-audience strategy.

title: Netflix content chief Bela Bajaria defines event strategy as streamer eyes more live sports
tldr: Netflix's content boss frames 'event' programming and live sports as the engine of engagement and cultural relevance. A window into how attention is being engineered at scale.
angle: The 'event' as a content pillar: what Netflix's live pivot teaches about engineering appointment attention.

title: Марина Вилле / Marina Willer crafts letters with light for BFI London Film Festival identity
tldr: Pentagram's analogue, light-projected identity for BFI pays homage to cinema's slow craft amid streaming and scattered viewing. A strong visual storytelling case in a fragmented-attention era.
why_fresh: design case, not a new trend
angle: Designing for slowness: crafting identity that resists scattergun viewing habits.

title: 5 Signs Your Financial Content Program Has a Credibility Problem
tldr: Contently argues AI engines and buyers now reward named, credentialed experts, and lists symptoms of a credibility gap. Ties expertise directly to AI-era content visibility.
angle: Why bylined human expertise is your best defense against AI-flattened content.

title: How the New York Jets extend OOH marketing for better storytelling
tldr: The Jets stretch out-of-home placements into a connected narrative rather than one-off ads. A tactical storytelling-across-channels case.
angle: Turning OOH from isolated billboards into a serialized brand story.
